root_cause: Depends and Security had been turned into plain @dataclass classes. A dataclass with eq=True and no frozen/unsafe_hash gets __hash__ = None, so hash(Depends(dep)) raised TypeError. That broke third-party tools such as Cadwyn, which relied on the objects being hashable (closed PR 14320). The obvious fix, frozen=True, has a knock-on effect: analyze_param in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py does `depends = copy(depends); depends.dependency = type_annotation` for the `x: Foo = Depends()` / `Annotated[Foo, Depends()]` class shortcut, and that line raises FrozenInstanceError once the class is frozen.
best_solution: In fastapi/params.py change `@dataclass` to `@dataclass(frozen=True)` on both Depends and its subclass Security. With eq=True, frozen=True makes Python generate a value-based __hash__ over the fields (dependency, use_cache, scope, plus scopes for Security), so equal instances hash equal and a different scope hashes differently. Then grep for code that mutates instances: analyze_param in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py assigns `depends.dependency = type_annotation` on a copy. Replace that with `depends = dataclasses.replace(depends, dependency=type_annotation)` and add `import dataclasses`. The patch also has to cover the mutation site, or the class-as-dependency shortcut breaks at route definition time.
acceptable_alternatives: `@dataclass(unsafe_hash=True)` on both classes passes the hidden test and keeps the objects mutable, so utils.py needs no change (this was option 2 in PR 14320). An explicit `__hash__` over (dependency, use_cache, scope[, scopes]) also works. Option 3 from PR 14320 (identity hash via object.__hash__) fails, because the test asserts hash(Depends(dep)) == hash(Depends(dep)) for two distinct instances. frozen=True without the dataclasses.replace change passes the hidden test but breaks `Depends()` with no argument.
hidden_test_demands: New tests/test_depends_hashable.py::test_depends_hashable: hash(Depends(dep)) == hash(Depends(dep)); hash(Security(dep)) == hash(Security(dep)); hash(Depends(dep)) != hash(Depends(dep, scope='function')); hash(Depends(dep, scope='function')) == hash(Depends(dep, scope='function')). So the hash must be value-based (identity hash fails) and must include the scope field. Only default scopes=None is exercised for Security. The hidden test does not cover the `Depends()` no-argument path.
locating_signals: The title names `Depends()` and `Security()`. Grepping `class Depends` finds fastapi/params.py, where both are bare `@dataclass`. That, plus the dataclass rule that eq without frozen sets __hash__ = None, gives the main fix. The second gold location (analyze_param in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py, `depends.dependency = type_annotation`) is not named anywhere. You only find it by grepping for assignments to Depends fields after freezing the class, or by running the existing suite (e.g. the tests for classes used as dependencies with `Depends()`).
our_outcome_summary: v4, v6, v7 and v8 all passed in the Kaggle env (47-84s, 12-23 calls). All four only changed the two decorators in fastapi/params.py to @dataclass(frozen=True). v8 also added a Security.__post_init__ that converts scopes to a tuple via object.__setattr__. None of them updated analyze_param in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py, which still runs `depends.dependency = type_annotation` on a frozen copy. That raises FrozenInstanceError for `x: Foo = Depends()` / `Annotated[Foo, Depends()]` (checked: assigning a field on a copied frozen dataclass raises `FrozenInstanceError: cannot assign to field 'dependency'`). The patches passed only because the grader runs just the hidden test file (log: 1 passed). If the full suite ran, they would regress.
generalizable_lesson: If you make a class immutable or hashable (dataclass frozen=True, NamedTuple, __slots__ with read-only properties), grep the whole package for attribute assignments on its instances (`\.<field>\s*=`, setattr, `copy(x); x.f = ...`) and rewrite them as dataclasses.replace(...) or a constructor call. Then run the existing tests that touch that class, not just the new one. For a 'make X hashable' request on a dataclass, remember that eq=True without frozen sets __hash__ = None. Choose frozen=True (value hash, but you must fix mutation sites) or unsafe_hash=True (value hash, stays mutable). Tests usually assert that equal-field instances hash equal, so an identity hash is not enough.
